title: BVAP: Energy and Memory Efficient Automata Processing for Regular Expressions with Bounded Repetitions
problem: Specialized in-memory automata processors lack efficient hardware support for bounded repetition constructs, which are widely used in regular expressions. This limitation constrains their practical applicability across pattern-matching domains.
motivation: Regular pattern matching is pervasive in text processing, malware detection, network security, and bioinformatics, making efficient automata processors critical infrastructure for these applications.
method: BVAP pairs a compiler with specialized hardware to efficiently process regular expressions. The compiler translates text-search patterns (including bounded repetitions—repeats with limits, like 'match between 1 and 5 times') into hardware-specific instructions. The hardware then uses bit vectors (where each bit represents whether a pattern is actively matching at that point) to run pattern matching directly in memory, cutting energy use and chip size.
key_novelty: The Action-Homogeneous Non-deterministic Bit Vector Automata (AH-NBVA) model enables hardware to efficiently support regular expression patterns with bounded repetitions (repeats capped at specific counts, like 1 to 5 times).
contributions: Novel AH-NBVA theoretical model for bounded repetition support
Hardware implementation of bit vector automata processor in 28nm CMOS
Compiler for translating regexes to hardware configurations
Demonstrated 67-95% higher energy efficiency and 42-68% lower area versus CA, eAP, CAMA
limitations: Hardware scalability constraints, applicability boundaries for complex regex patterns, and practical deployment challenges are not discussed.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient in-memory automata processing for regex
